issues.legal_issue: A proceeding to settle a management scheme for a public trust does not abate merely because an applicant dies or is not substituted, and the decision-maker may allow late substitution or add interested persons.
material_facts: A scheme proceeding was initiated on a prescribed application made by two persons interested in a public trust.
One applicant died while the proceeding was pending, and the deceased applicant’s son applied several years later to join the proceeding, asserting an interest in the trust.
The decision-maker allowed the son to join and also allowed two other persons, found to be interested in the trust, to join as applicants.
issues.conclusion: The proceeding did not abate because of the applicant’s death or the delay in substitution; the decision-maker had power to allow late substitution and to add interested persons.
issues.legal_principle: Section 50A of the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950 permits the Charity Commissioner to initiate a scheme proceeding on the prescribed written application of two or more persons interested in a public trust, as well as suo motu where the statutory conditions are met. The proceeding serves the proper management and administration of the trust and is not defeated by the death, withdrawal, or non-substitution of an applicant. Rule 7 of the Bombay Public Trust Rules, 1951 concerns the manner of inquiry, not the initiation of the proceeding or the Commissioner’s substantive authority. Procedural law is subservient to substantive law and should aid, not defeat, its object. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.public_trust_scheme_inquiry: The decision-maker is considering a scheme for the proper management or administration of a public trust.
predicates.valid_initiation_by_interested_applicant: Two or more persons interested in the trust initiated the proceeding by a prescribed written application.
predicates.applicant_dies_or_withdraws: An applicant dies or withdraws before the proceeding is concluded.

issues.definition: When a properly initiated public-trust scheme inquiry continues after an applicant dies or withdraws, the proceeding does not abate and late substitution or addition may be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: The Civil Procedure Code does not automatically govern a scheme inquiry before the public-trust decision-maker merely because the inquiry rules refer to Small Causes Court procedure.
material_facts: The proceeding was an inquiry before the Charity Commissioner to consider settling a management scheme for a public trust.

The appellant relied on Rule 7 of the Bombay Public Trust Rules, 1951, and Section 6 of the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882, to argue that the Civil Procedure Code applied and that non-substitution caused abatement.

Rule 7 directed that inquiries be conducted, as far as possible, according to the procedure for Small Causes Court suits; Section 6 treated the Small Causes Court as a court for specified purposes, while Section 9 addressed the prescription of its procedure.
issues.conclusion: The Civil Procedure Code did not apply to the proceeding on the basis of Rule 7 and Section 6; the argument that the proceeding abated under that Code was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 7 of the Bombay Public Trust Rules, 1951 provides that specified inquiries are to be held, as far as possible, according to Small Causes Court procedure. Section 6 of the Presidency Small Cause Courts Act, 1882 refers to the status of the Small Causes Court for specified legal purposes; it does not prescribe the procedure for its suits. Section 9 provides for procedure to be prescribed by High Court rules. Accordingly, those references do not make the Civil Procedure Code applicable to a proceeding before the Charity Commissioner. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

predicates.administrative_trust_scheme_inquiry: The proceeding is an inquiry before an administrative decision-maker considering a management scheme for a public trust.
predicates.inquiry_rule_refers_to_small_cause_proce: The inquiry rule directs the decision-maker to follow Small Causes Court procedure only as far as possible.
predicates.court_status_reference_does_not_prescrib: A legal reference to the Small Causes Court concerns its status for specified purposes and does not itself prescribe its trial procedure.
predicates.procedure_is_set_separately: The procedure for the Small Causes Court is prescribed through a separate rulemaking mechanism.

issues.definition: When an administrative public-trust scheme inquiry is subject to a qualified procedural reference, the court-status reference does not prescribe trial procedure, and procedure is set separately, the Civil Procedure Code does not automatically govern the inquiry.
